proposals.evidence: Turner 2575 explicitly cites European Romani kon 'who' and, in its addendum, an oblique kɔs in a Pahari paradigm. The source prints Zargari kon/qon (nominative), kos/qos (oblique), kosku (dative/genitive), kostār (ablative/instrumental), and kostu (locative) together in §3.3.5.1, plus indefinite kon/qon 'somebody' in §3.3.6.1 (p. 136). The case endings and indefinite use are source-level morphology of the same inherited pronoun; no distinct etymon is inferred for each case form. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

proposals.evidence: Turner 14108 §2 expressly lists Romani Italian yidž and Hungarian īž/ič as 'yesterday' under *hīyas. The source prints ij/iž as the Zargari word for 'yesterday' (§2.3.21 and §3.20.1.2, pp. 128, 143); its pronunciation discussion accounts for the imported glyph variant. The section-2 etymon is the precise parent. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

proposals.evidence: Turner 5731 §1 gives European Romani tel, tele 'under' and other Indo-Aryan bottom/below forms under tala. The source prints Zargari teli as 'bottom' (§3.1.15, p. 132), 'below' (§3.20.1.3, p. 143), and 'beneath; under' (§3.20.2.1, p. 144), supporting all three lexical/syntactic attestations. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.
